clause.quote:
Most of NOAA's information is in the ‘public domain’ and CANNOT be copyrighted. **Unless otherwise noted in the credit or caption of the item** of interest, you may use it without express permission. The one exception are our videos, as they often use third-party copyrighted footage. Video, in other words, will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. However, for most other content (e.g., our images, infographics, articles) you may use this material, but may not:

- Claim it as your own (i.e., claiming copyright for federal information);
- Use it in a manner that implies an endorsement or affiliation with the U.S. Government; or
- Modify the content or misrepresent the content, and then present it as official government material.

Credit should be given to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

policies.judgement: 官方默认许可并保留具体credit/caption例外；视频第三方镜头按件处理。署名、无政府背书、不把修改内容冒称官方原文。不能从视频例外直接推出所有原作播客音频都被禁用。

clause.quote:
Works of the U.S. federal government are generally not protected by copyright in the United States and are automatically in the public domain (17 USC§ 105). No permission is required to reuse, reprint, or distribute this material, however, proper attribution and citation should be applied.

This also applies to photographs and videos that NOAA or any federal agency would be considered the owner of.

That is to say if the image, video, or article in question appears to be a NOAA-only (or Federal agency-only) published item, it's safe to assume it's public domain. You do not need to ask permission to use it, but you do need to attribute and cite it.

If any other authorship appears (such as a Cooperative Institute, university, etc.), you cannot assume it's public domain and you will need to check with all potential copyright holders.

policies.judgement: 官方明示美国联邦原作可再用/再印/分发，并允许根据NOAA-only公开作品判断；出现大学/合作机构等其他作者时另核。此为实际政策支持，不增设未披露私人guest release/cue sheet要求。

clause.quote: The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is a Federal government agency and everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations. clause.quote:
## Copyright Policy

### Can I copy and reuse information on the NIMH website?

Yes, unless otherwise indicated, text on the NIMH website and in NIMH materials may be copied and reused.

- **Permission to copy**: The information on our website and in our materials is in the public domain. You may copy and reuse it without permission.
- **Modifications**: You can edit or reformat the copied text, but you cannot change it in a way that is misleading or inaccurate.
- **Attribution**: If you use our information or publications, please [cite the National Institute of Mental Health](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/site-info/citing-nimh-publications-and-webpages) as the source.
- **Linking**: We update our information regularly. We encourage you to link to our content rather than copy it to ensure users always have the most up-to-date information.

### Can I copy and reuse images on the NIMH website?

No, you may not copy or reuse images on the NIMH website or in our materials, even if you cite them.

Most of the images on our website are stock photos of professional models. We use these photos to add visual interest to the website, and you cannot reuse these images for any purpose.

### Can I reuse the information and images in NIMH publications?

[Esta información también está disponible en español](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/espanol/reproduccion-y-reutilizacion-de-las-publicaciones-del-nimh)

Like the website, the information in [NIMH publications](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications) is in the public domain and may be reused or copied without permission. We encourage you to use our fact sheets, brochures, and infographics to improve public health. Please [cite the National Institute of Mental Health](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/site-info/citing-nimh-publications-and-webpages) as the source.

Please note: You may not reuse or copy any of the publication images.

Since it is unlawful to misuse government materials, we ask that you follow these guidelines when using our publications:

- Do not change the content of our publications in a way that is misleading or inaccurate.
- Do not add logos to our publications.
- Do not copy or reuse images in our publications, even if you cite them.
- Do not use our publications to advertise or endorse products, processes, or services.
- Do not use our publications to give the appearance of providing specific medical advice, treatment recommendations, or referrals.
- Whenever possible, link to our publications instead of downloading them to ensure users always have the most up-to-date information.

policies.judgement: NIMH文字除另注外可复制再用，可编辑但不误导，署名；图片不可再用，不作医疗建议/治疗推荐或商业背书。该候选只作语言理解，不要求个人诊断/披露。
